marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q001.takeaway: Horner findings after upper thoracic sympathetic interruption can follow injury to the T1 white ramus, which carries preganglionic inflow to the sympathetic chain.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q001.displayText: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Horner's or Bernard-Horner's syndrome. It can be caused by a lesion of the white ramus of T1. Horner's syndrome is characterized by a constricted pupil (miosis), drooping of the upper eyelid (ptosis), and absence of sweating of the face (anhidrosis), due to disruption of sympathetic nerve supply. In the autonomic nervous system, the sympathetic outflow is thoracolumbar and parasympathetic outflow is craniosacral. The sympathetic chain receives white ramus inflow (preganglionic fibers) and gives gray ramus outflow (postganglionic fibers); white rami occur from T1-L2. In this setting sympathetic inflow at T1 is disrupted.
emphasis: The given clinical scenario is suggestive of Horner's or Bernard-Horner's syndrome
It can be caused by a lesion of the white ramus of T1

Horner's syndrome is characterized by a constricted pupil (miosis), drooping of the upper eyelid (ptosis), and absence of sweating of the face (anhidrosis), due to disruption of sympathetic nerve supply

rationales.a: The gray ramus carries postganglionic sympathetic fibers from chain back to spinal nerves; it is not the preganglionic inflow pathway described.
rationales.c: A gray ramus at C8 would not carry the thoracolumbar preganglionic outflow; the source localizes this pattern to T1 white ramus.
rationales.d: White rami exist from T1 through L2, not at C8.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q002.takeaway: Brachial-plexus divisions do not give branches; roots, trunks and cords each give named branches.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q002.displayText: The divisions in the brachial plexus do not give any branches. The roots, trunks, and cords of the brachial plexus give direct branches.
emphasis: The divisions in the brachial plexus do not give any branches
The roots, trunks, and cords of the brachial plexus give direct branches

rationales.a: Roots give dorsal scapular and long thoracic nerves among other branches.
rationales.b: Cords give collateral branches as well as terminal nerves.
rationales.c: Trunks give suprascapular nerve and nerve to subclavius from the superior trunk.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q003.takeaway: Plexus arterial supply comes from subclavian and vertebral branches, not the common carotids; the other statements fit the source.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q003.displayText: Arterial supply to the brachial plexus is from branches of the subclavian and vertebral arteries, not the common carotid arteries. The superior trunk gives the suprascapular nerve (C5, C6) and nerve to subclavius (C5, C6). The radial nerve (C5-T1) is the largest branch of the plexus and arises as a terminal branch of the posterior cord. Variations include a C4 pre-fixed plexus and T2 post-fixed plexus.
emphasis: Arterial supply to the brachial plexus is from branches of the subclavian and vertebral arteries, not the common carotid arteries
The superior trunk gives the suprascapular nerve (C5, C6) and nerve to subclavius (C5, C6)
The radial nerve (C5-T1) is the largest branch of the plexus and arises as a terminal branch of the posterior cord

rationales.a: The nerve to subclavius arises from the superior trunk.
rationales.c: The radial nerve is the largest brachial-plexus branch.
rationales.d: A prefixed plexus can receive C4 contribution.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q004.takeaway: An infraclavicular block targets cords and their branches, including the thoracodorsal nerve; supraclavicular branches arise above this level.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q004.displayText: The thoracodorsal nerve would be anesthetized by an infraclavicular block because it is an infraclavicular branch arising from the posterior cord (C6-C8). Branches arising from roots and trunks are supraclavicular: dorsal scapular nerve (C5), long thoracic nerve of Bell, suprascapular nerve, and nerve to subclavius (C5, C6). Other branches arising from the cords are infraclavicular.

rationales.a: The nerve to subclavius branches from the superior trunk above the clavicle.
rationales.b: The dorsal scapular nerve usually branches from C5 root in the neck.
rationales.c: The long thoracic nerve arises from roots and descends on the thoracic wall, proximal to the infraclavicular block.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q005.takeaway: Upper-trunk C5–C6 injury causes Erb palsy with shoulder adduction and medial rotation; abduction is lost rather than produced.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q005.displayText: Upper trunk injury causes Erb or Erb-Duchenne palsy. It produces adduction and medial rotation at the shoulder, not abduction. The usual mechanism is excessive separation of head and neck, including birth injury, damaging C5-C6. Affected nerves include suprascapular, axillary, musculocutaneous, and radial nerves. The classic waiter's-tip posture includes arm adducted and medially rotated, elbow extended, forearm pronated, and sensory loss along the outer aspect of the arm.
emphasis: Upper trunk injury causes Erb or Erb-Duchenne palsy
It produces adduction and medial rotation at the shoulder, not abduction
The usual mechanism is excessive separation of head and neck, including birth injury, damaging C5-C6

rationales.a: Adduction is part of the classic waiters-tip posture.
rationales.b: Forearm pronation is compatible with the classic posture.
rationales.d: Sensory loss over the outer arm is a recognized C5–C6 sensory finding.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q006.takeaway: The axillary nerve is the surgeon’s nerve and can be injured by an improperly placed deltoid intramuscular injection.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q006.displayText: The axillary nerve, also called the surgeon's nerve, may be injured during inadvertent intramuscular injection. It is a branch of the posterior cord, exits the axilla through the quadrangular space, winds around the surgical neck of the humerus, and gives upper lateral cutaneous nerve of arm supply over the lower deltoid. Injury can follow surgical-neck fracture, inferior shoulder dislocation, or IM injection and may cause regimental-badge anesthesia. Named nerves listed by the source: labourer's nerve = median nerve; musician's nerve = ulnar nerve; surgeon's nerve = axillary nerve; nerve of Bell = long thoracic nerve.

rationales.c: The long thoracic nerve is the nerve of Bell and supplies serratus anterior.
rationales.d: The ulnar nerve is called the musician’s nerve.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q007.takeaway: Median nerve has no close humeral landmark; axillary, ulnar and radial nerves relate respectively to surgical neck, medial epicondyle and radial groove.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q007.displayText: The median nerve is not directly related to the humerus. The axillary nerve is related to the surgical neck, the ulnar nerve to the medial epicondyle, and the radial nerve to the spiral/radial groove. The median nerve arises from lateral and medial cords, gives no muscular branch in the axilla and arm, supplies most superficial flexors in the forearm, passes between the two heads of pronator teres and gives the anterior interosseous nerve, gives a palmar cutaneous branch before the flexor retinaculum, and divides distally into recurrent and palmar digital branches.

rationales.a: The axillary nerve winds around the surgical neck of the humerus.
rationales.c: The ulnar nerve passes behind the medial epicondyle.
rationales.d: The radial nerve lies in the spiral groove along the posterior humerus.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q008.takeaway: Abductor pollicis brevis contraction tests the median recurrent motor branch at the wrist; the palmar cutaneous territory is usually spared in carpal tunnel lesions.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q008.displayText: Median nerve injury at the wrist is tested by contraction of abductor pollicis brevis; loss of thumb mobility/opposition can be tested by the pen test. Flexor pollicis brevis paralysis may occur with median nerve injury at the arm/elbow. Benediction-hand and Ochsner clasping tests are used for more proximal median lesions. The lateral half of the palm is supplied by the palmar cutaneous branch and is usually spared in carpal tunnel/wrist lesions because the branch does not pass through the carpal tunnel. Ring-finger sensation is not an isolated median-nerve test.
emphasis: Median nerve injury at the wrist is tested by contraction of abductor pollicis brevis; loss of thumb mobility/opposition can be tested by the pen test
Flexor pollicis brevis paralysis may occur with median nerve injury at the arm/elbow
Benediction-hand and Ochsner clasping tests are used for more proximal median lesions

rationales.a: Flexor pollicis brevis may be affected by a more proximal median lesion; it is not the best wrist-level test given here.
rationales.b: Sensation across the palm is not lost with a wrist lesion because the palmar cutaneous branch arises proximal to the tunnel.
rationales.d: The ring finger has overlapping median/ulnar sensory supply and is not the focal median wrist test.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q009.takeaway: Ape-thumb deformity can follow median-nerve lesions at different levels because thenar denervation leads to distal wasting; adductor pollicis and medial FDP are ulnar supplied.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q009.displayText: The marked sensory territory is supplied by the median nerve. Ape-thumb deformity is seen with median nerve lesions irrespective of site because it reflects distal denervation and non-use atrophy of the thenar muscles except adductor pollicis. The median nerve supplies the superficial flexor group except flexor carpi ulnaris and the medial half of flexor digitorum profundus; its anterior interosseous branch supplies flexor pollicis longus, pronator quadratus, and lateral half of FDP; recurrent branch supplies thenar muscles except adductor pollicis; palmar digital branches supply the lateral two lumbricals and skin of the lateral 3½ digits. Adductor pollicis and medial half of FDP are ulnar supplied, while wrist drop is a radial-nerve palsy.

rationales.a: Adductor pollicis is supplied by the deep branch of the ulnar nerve.
rationales.b: The medial half of FDP is ulnar supplied; median/AIN supplies its lateral half.
rationales.d: Wrist drop is characteristic of radial-nerve palsy, not median-nerve injury.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q010.takeaway: Median-nerve injury at the cubital fossa can impair palmar sensation of the index nail bed through its digital branches.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q010.displayText: The structure marked A is the median nerve in the cubital fossa. Median nerve lesion causes loss of sensation of the nail of the index finger. Median cutaneous supply includes the lateral two-thirds of the palm by its superficial cutaneous branch and the lateral 3½ fingers on the palmar surface plus dorsal nail beds by palmar digital nerves. The source mnemonic for cubital-fossa contents from medial to lateral is MBBR: median nerve, brachial artery, biceps brachii tendon, radial nerve.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q011.takeaway: Palmar interossei are ulnar-innervated and are vulnerable in an elbow-level ulnar lesion.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q011.displayText: The ulnar nerve supplies the palmar interossei. It arises from the medial cord, supplies no muscle in the axilla or arm, runs medial to the brachial artery to mid-arm, then passes posteromedially through the medial intermuscular septum and arcade of Struthers. In the upper forearm it passes between the two heads of flexor carpi ulnaris, gives a dorsal cutaneous branch distally, crosses the wrist superficial to the flexor retinaculum through Guyon's tunnel, and distal to the pisiform divides into superficial and deep terminal branches.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q012.takeaway: The described intrinsic weakness and inability to hold paper localize to the ulnar nerve at the medial epicondyle, marked C in the figure.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q012.displayText: The presentation is of ulnar nerve injury; the most likely site shown is the medial epicondyle (marked C). Ulnar lesions may produce a positive card test, claw hand deformity, Froment's sign, Wartenberg sign, and palmaris brevis sign. A positive card test reflects weakness of palmar interossei and impaired finger adduction. In the source figure, A is the radial groove (radial nerve with profunda brachii), D is the surgical neck (axillary nerve), and B is the lateral epicondyle; C corresponds to the medial epicondyle.

rationales.b: The lateral epicondyle (B) is not the ulnar nerve passage behind the medial epicondyle.
rationales.d: The surgical neck (D) is associated with axillary nerve injury.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q013.takeaway: Hypothenar atrophy plus palmar little-finger numbness implicates the ulnar nerve before its superficial and deep terminal branches separate.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q013.displayText: The findings indicate an ulnar nerve lesion before division into superficial and deep terminal branches because functions of both branches are affected. Distal to the pisiform, the superficial branch supplies palmaris brevis and skin of the palmar medial 1½ fingers; the deep branch runs with the deep palmar arch and supplies the intrinsic hand muscles except the first two lumbricals and thenar muscles. The source compares high elbow lesions with low wrist/Guyon's canal lesions and illustrates Froment testing.

rationales.d: An isolated superficial-branch lesion explains skin numbness but not hypothenar motor atrophy.

marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q014.takeaway: Thumb adduction/card test depends on adductor pollicis, supplied by the deep ulnar branch in the palm.
marrow__ANAT_CH38_Q014.displayText: Loss of thumb adduction points to injury of the deep branch of the ulnar nerve. The hypothenar wound can interrupt the branch before it reaches adductor pollicis. The deep branch initially supplies hypothenar muscles, then interossei and third/fourth lumbricals, and ends by supplying adductor pollicis and the medial/deep head of flexor pollicis brevis. It also sends articular filaments to the wrist joint.

rationales.a: The superficial terminal branch chiefly supplies palmaris brevis and digital sensation, not adductor pollicis.
rationales.c: The deep radial branch supplies posterior forearm extensors, not thumb adduction.
rationales.d: The deep median branch is not the motor supply to adductor pollicis.
